entertainment.title: Phil Collins Walks With 2 Canes During Rare Public Appearance
entertainment.summary: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame marked another day in paradise for Phil Collins fans. After all, the beloved rocker made an ultra-rare public appearance for the Nov. 14 induction ceremony in Los...
entertainment.body:
The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame marked another day in paradise for Phil Collins fans.

After all, the beloved rocker made an ultra-rare public appearance for the Nov. 14 induction ceremony in Los Angeles, marking his first major event since May amid his ongoing health challenges.

For the occasion—which saw Collins inducted as a solo member, having previously been included as part of Genesis 2010—the 75-year-old walked the carpet in an elegant black suit which he paired with a white button-down shirt, the collar of which he left loose, and with the assistance of two wooden canes.

Collins was joined for the evening by three of his five children; Joely Collins , 54, whom he shares with ex-wife Andrea Bertorelli ; Lily Collins , 37, whom he shares with ex-wife Jill Tavelman ; and Nicholas Collins , 25, whom he shares with ex-wife Orianne Cevey . (The drummer is also dad to Simon Collins , 50, with Bertorelli and Matthew Collins , 22, with Cevey.)

In fact, during his speech on stage, Collins proved there will always be gratitude in his heart for his former wives, reserving a special shoutout for them.

"They loved me through the years, but more importantly, they have given me five great children," he said, per USA Today . "They are incredibly talented, and I made life tough for them growing up. But they have turned into such wonderful human beings. I love them to death."

The “Son of Man” artist—who in recent years has been navigating challenges with his kidneys, nerves and spine, in addition to type-2 diabetes—also took a moment to address his health after first taking to the stage.

“Thank you so much, I'm really not as bad as it looks," he told the audience, holding his canes aloft. "I'm much better."

entertainment.title: Why Morgan Fairchild Ignored Her Agents And Took A Low-Paying Job On A Hit Sitcom
entertainment.summary: When the right opportunity shows up, you have to take it. That's what Morgan Fairchild did when offered a lower-paying role on a sitcom she knew would be a hit.
entertainment.body:
Produced by "Laverne & Shirley" creator Garry Marshall, ABC's "Mork & Mindy" was a runaway sci-fi sitcom hit that skyrocketed a then-unknown Williams to superstardom. The series — which was a "Happy Days" spin-off — followed Mork (Williams), an eccentric extraterrestrial sent from the planet Ork to observe human behavior, who lands in Boulder, Colorado, and moves in with a free-spirited earthling named Mindy McConnell, played by Pam Dawber. Amid the cosmic chaos, Fairchild dropped in for a three-episode stint during the show's first season as Susan Taylor, Mindy's stuck-up high school frenemy.

During an exclusive interview with Entertainment Weekly , the "Dallas" alum recalled a phone call where her agent tried to deter her from an offer to guest star on a mysterious project that Marshall had "under wraps." "He doesn't want to give you a contract, and you'll only be recurring, and he only wants to pay you top-of-show, and you're making so much more money than that. Now we just think you should turn it down," Fairchild told the outlet. Fairchild, however, had other ideas. "I said, 'Well, what's the name of the show?' And he said, 'Mork & Mindy,' and I said, 'That's Robin Williams' show,' and he said, 'Who's Robin Williams?'" She continued, holding firm on her decision, "I said, 'Robin Williams is a genius. Don't tell Garry [but] I'd work for free to work with Robin Williams. I'll take the show.'"

ABC As to why Williams' involvement compelled Fairchild to sign the dotted line so quickly, it's because she had already witnessed the birth of Mork from Ork. After guest-starring on "Happy Days" in 1977, she frequently visited the Paramount lot. One day, Henry Winkler urged her to watch a particular guest star do his thing. That ended up being Williams' debut as Mork on the "Happy Days" episode "My Favorite Orkan." When the episode wrapped, Fairchild recalled to Entertainment Weekly: "I stayed all afternoon just to tell this guy he's a genius."

Fast-forward to her first "Mork & Mindy" episode, "Mork's Seduction," Fairchild noticed that Williams' wild comedic style altered how rehearsals ran under director Howie Storm. "Robin just goes, and everybody just stands back and watches Robin go," she explained. Rather than standing back, Fairchild let loose and spouted out unscripted banter right along with him during their scene. "Robin throws something out, and I throw something out, and he looks at me in shock ... and we're going back and forth," she recalled. "And, finally, he grabs me by the waist and, like, pushes me in the air and says, 'Mama, you're one of me.'"

entertainment.title: John Mulaney's Latest SNL Musical Brings Back Bowen Yang As Mary Todd Lincoln, Plus Ashley Padilla's Kathy
entertainment.summary: John Mulaney's latest SNL musical sketch features Bowen Yang as Mary Todd Lincoln and Ashley Padilla as annoying work colleague Kathy.
entertainment.body:
John Mulaney returned to "Saturday Night Live" this weekend, and you know what that means: another elaborate musical tribute to New York City, complete with Broadway parodies, eccentric characters, and a few familiar faces.

In the November 14 episode, Mulaney played a Central Park carriage driver lamenting the city's decision to ban horse-drawn carriages. As he escorted two tourists (Marcello Hernández and Kam Patterson) through the park, they encountered an assortment of New Yorkers, each with a song to sing.

Highlights included Veronika Slowikowska as a marathon runner who still hadn't finished the race, belting out a parody of "Don't Rain on My Parade" from "Funny Girl," and Tommy Brennan as a pedicab driver challenging Mulaney to "Anything You Can Do" from "Annie Get Your Gun." Elsewhere, Kenan Thompson appeared as a cloud of marijuana smoke in a number inspired by "Cats," while James Austin Johnson and Jeremy Culhane riffed on "West Side Story" as a Mayor Zohran Mamdani supporter and disgruntled billionaire, respectively.

But the biggest surprise came courtesy of former cast member Bowen Yang, currently starring in Broadway's "Oh, Mary!" Yang reprised his role as Mary Todd Lincoln — or, more specifically, the Mary Todd Lincoln Tunnel — performing a traffic-themed rendition of "And I Am Telling You I'm Not Going" from "Dreamgirls." It marked Yang's second appearance of the evening, following his return in the cold open as disgraced former NVIDIA CEO Jensen "Hide Your Wife" Huang.

Also surprising audiences was Ashley Padilla's Kathy, the socially oblivious office worker who had already made her second-ever appearance earlier that night, following her debut in last season's Jack Black-hosted episode .

NBC Mulaney's Broadway-inspired sketches date back to his first hosting stint in April 2018 , when Pete Davidson's decision to order seafood at a diner gave rise to "Diner Lobster," a parody of "Les Misérables." That was followed by " Bodega Bathroom " (2019), " Airport Sushi " (2020), " New York Musical " (2020), " Subway Churro " (2022), and " Port Authority Duane Reade " (2024).

The tradition continued during February 2025's "SNL50" anniversary special, when Mulaney led a star-studded musical tribute to New York City featuring Lin-Manuel Miranda, Nathan Lane, and several returning cast members.

entertainment.title: Robert Christgau and Carola Dibbell Talk New Documentary ‘The Last Critic’ and Staying Crazy in Love
entertainment.summary: A new film focuses on the legendary music critic. It’s also a portrait of a rock & roll marriage that's lasted more than 50 years
entertainment.body:
The Last Critic is one of the year’s most fascinating rock documentaries — even though it’s not about a musician. It’s a portrait of the legendary writer Robert Christgau , the self-proclaimed “Dean of American Rock Critics.” He was one of the pioneers who invented pop-music criticism in the Sixties — but six decades later, at 83, he’s still at the top of the game. He began his Consumer Guide column in the Village Voice in 1969, and has kept cranking it out ever since, now on Substack . For generations of music fanatics, Christgau’s voice hits like Bob Dylan or Neil Young — two artists his age who are still doing it with the same fiercely independent spirit he brings to his writing.

The debut feature from director Matty Wishnow, The Last Critic won the jury prize at the South by Southwest and Oak Cliff Film festivals, as well as the 2026 Screen Dallas grand prize. It gets its New York premiere tomorrow. The film, which is co-produced by longtime Rolling Stone contributor and editor Joe Levy, goes beyond music, because it’s also the portrait of a marriage. Christgau and his wife, novelist Carola Dibbell , have been together more than 50 years. Over the decades, they’ve shared an intellectual life, raised their daughter, collected way too much vinyl, and — the weirdest part — remained crazy in love.

Christgau has a fearsome rep for never pulling his punches, with his own savage wit. Lou Reed spent a chunk of his live album Take No Prisoners complaining about getting a B+ grade for Street Hassl e ; when U2 won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year in 1988 for The Joshua Tree , Bono jokily groused in his speech about his band’s reviews in the Village Voice. Christgau’s inspired more songs attacking him than any other journalist, from Sonic Youth (“Kill Yr Idols”) to Public Enemy (“Bring the Noise”).

But there’s something obsessive about his lifelong quest to chronicle the music, still going strong after 60 years — he’s heard more albums than anyone on the planet. When he reviewed Prince ’s Dirty Mind in 1980, he dropped one of the most-quoted one-liners in critical history: “Mick Jagger can fold up his penis and go home.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

The Last Critic features artists Christgau has reviewed, as well as writers he’s inspired, from Sonic Youth’s Thurston Moore to Pulitzer-winning novelist Colson Whitehead. (I make an appearance as well.) There’s a touching interlude with his lifelong friend Greil Marcus, the only other OG rock critic who’s kept doing it this long (or this well). In one of the most surprising moments, the legendary songwriter Randy Newman recalls their friendship, and admits he wrote a song about Christgau and Dibbell, “Lost Without You,” inspired by the closeness of their marriage. It’s the kind of movie where you come for the rock, stay for the romance.

entertainment.title: 5 Forgotten Christmas Specials Worth Revisiting This Holiday Season
entertainment.summary: From Judy Garland and Dolly Parton to the Muppets, these forgotten Christmas specials are well worth revisiting for some old-fashioned festive entertainment.
entertainment.body:
ABC/YouTube Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover While every streaming platform offers vast libraries of Christmas content each holiday season, one seasonal tradition is missing: the Christmas special. Though they still exist on streamers , we mean old-fashioned Christmas specials that aired on broadcast television and delighted audiences. From classic variety shows to beloved animated shorts, these programs made the Christmas season special.

Thankfully, not all of these specials have been lost to time. We all have access to a little website called YouTube, which contains a massive archive of forgotten TV content. We've trawled YouTube for the best Christmas specials to watch this holiday season. You may have seen some of these and forgotten about them, while others may be new discoveries. Either way, these old-school Christmas specials ought to bring a little holiday magic to your festivities.

Channel 4/YouTube Though Raymond Briggs' "The Snowman" has become a holiday favorite in the United Kingdom , it's less well-known stateside (despite a flashy introduction meant to entice American audiences). Based on Briggs' 1978 picture book, "The Snowman" is a wordless, animated TV special that follows a boy and a snowman that has come to life. Beautifully drawn and featuring an evocative, orchestral score, the special is both heartwarming and melancholic. Its most famous sequence depicts the boy and the snowman flying together over snowy landscapes, while it ends with the snowman's inevitable demise.

"The Snowman" first broadcast on the UK's Channel 4 in 1982, the first year of that network's existence, and has aired every year since. When the special's producers wanted to sell the film to U.S. distributors, they brought David Bowie on board to record an intro (Briggs did the original introduction). The special was nominated for Best Short Film, Animated, in 1983, though it lost to Zbigniew Rybczyński's "Tango." You can now watch "The Snowman" on YouTube, with either David Bowie's intro or the original Burr introduction .

The plot in "A Muppet Family Christmas" is almost nonexistent, but that's totally fine—the joy of the film is watching these characters interact. Fozzie Bear takes his friends to stay at his mom's farmhouse, not knowing Doc from "Fraggle Rock" is already there. The cast of "Sesame Street" also shows up — no explanation needed — and hilarity ensues. The Swedish Chef tries to cook Big Bird. Miss Piggy gets lost in a snowstorm. Fozzie befriends a snowman.

entertainment.title: Wu-Tang Clan, Billy Idol, Phil Collins Enter Rock Hall at All-Star Induction Ceremony
entertainment.summary: Bearded Red Hot Chili Peppers honor Rick Rubin, U2 serve as surprise openers, Aerosmith and Run-D.M.C. reunite, Oprah Winfrey inducts Luther Vandross and more
entertainment.body:
It was difficult to imagine who could possibly top Wu-Tang Clan ’s performance at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction on Saturday night at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater. Following a spirited introduction from Chris Rock, all living members of the Staten Island hip-hop group hit the stage to perform a medley of some of their biggest hits, including “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” The audience was on its collective feet screaming “Wu-Tang! Wu-Tang!” repeatedly as the mighty crew wielded their lyrical swords.

But then came the Red Hot Chili Peppers, who were part of Rick Rubin ’s induction. Cosplaying Rubin (who, after an incredibly theatrical induction speech by Neil Young, accepted his honor in shorts, sandals and rose-tinted sunglasses), Anthony Kiedis, John Frusciante, Flea and Chad Smith erupted into their Blood Sugar Sex Magik single “Give It Away” donning fake white beards. After a short technical issue with Flea’s instrument, the ever-limber bassist and Kiedis continued to somehow defy aging and rocked it like it was 1991.

The high octane performances kept coming at a dizzying pace. The speeches were long (sans Rubin) and the event as usual ran well over four hours. But as Wu-Tang Clan and Rubin joined fellow honorees Queen Latifah, New Order / Joy Division , MC Lyte, Billy Idol , Iron Maiden , Luther Vandross, Sade , Oasis , Phil Collins , Celia Cruz, Fela Kuti, Gram Parsons, Linda Creed, Arif Mardin and Jimmy Miller, the excitement of “what’s next” made time disappear.

Of course several inductees opted not to show up (Oasis, New Order’s Bernard Sumner, Gillian Gilbert and Stephen Morris, Sade and Iron Maiden) and some of them were being inducted posthumously, but the Rock Hall was still able to make the evening magical with surprise presenters and performances.

entertainment.title: The '80s Fantasy Drama Series That Made Ron Perlman A Star Also Nearly Ruined His Career

entertainment.body:
In a 2011 interview with ComingSoon , Perlman explained how his initial roles being makeup-heavy led to uncertainty about the kind of roles he could be cast in: "It took a while for people to figure out what kind of roles to let me play. ... The first movie I was in was 'Quest for Fire.' The second was 'In the Name of the Rose .' ... I was very much covered up by special effects makeup. Then came 'Beauty and the Beast' and there was no indication of 'who is Ron Perlman and what does he do? What does he give off?'"

Created by Ron Koslow and produced by George R.R. Martin, "Beauty and the Beast" takes a modern approach to the famous romantic story. After New York attorney Catherine Chandler (Linda Hamilton) is assaulted in the streets, half-lion, half-man Vincent (Perlman) rescues her and takes her to a hidden underground utopia. As he nurses her back to health, the two develop a deep relationship.

CBS Although initially being typecast as Vincent led to his career stumbling for a few years, Ron Perlman has nothing but affection for the character. He told one interviewer, "Vincent was the most unique character that ever was on television" (via TikTok ). The character won him a Golden Globe for best performance by an actor in a drama series in 1989, and he was nominated for two Emmys for outstanding lead actor in a drama series in 1988 and 1989.

Perlman credits his career success to two particular directors. "There are two guys who are responsible for my career: Jean-Jacques Annaud and Guillermo [del Toro]," Perlman told Cigar Aficionado. "They both showed up at the lowest times, when I began to consider that I had reached the end of my run but didn't know where I was going."

In 1992, he first collaborated with del Toro on "Cronos," before starring in "Blade II," "Hellboy," and "Pacific Rim" years later. In 2001, he starred in Annaud's "Enemy at the Gates," although he had already worked with Annaud prior to "Beauty and the Beast" on "The Name of the Rose" and "Quest for Fire." His relationship with del Toro in particular helped him regain prominence, as he revealed in an interview with A.V. Club : "I actually have no doubt in my mind that him winning me the role of Hellboy has completely transformed the shape and trajectory of my life and career."

Created by George Kay and François Uzan and first released on the streamer in 2021, this exquisitely assembled crime thriller reached a huge global crowd with its mastery of twists, turns, punctilious character work, and refined heist sequences. And it's still going strong on its recently released Part 4.

If you're already burned through the new batch of "Lupin" episodes, as one tends to be compelled to do upon watching just one or two installments of this highly binge-worthy show, fret not. While there's no official word yet on whether there will be a "Lupin" Season 5 and how soon we can expect it, there are numerous other great shows in a similar ballpark that you can watch to sate your craving for more of Assane's Parisian adventures. Below, you'll find a list of 10 other impeccable heist-centric shows that might be of interest if you love "Lupin."

Netflix When it comes to foreign-language, heist-themed hit Netflix shows, no recommendation for "Lupin" fans is more of a no-brainer than "Money Heist." Originally aired on Spanish local network Antena 3 before moving to Netflix for its latter two seasons (with the streamer also handling the first season's international distribution in a re-cut version), this Álex Pina-created series charts the intricate, multi-layered mayhem that unfolds when a mysterious man known only as the Professor (Álvaro Morte) recruits eight anonymous strangers — each referred to only by a city name chosen as an alias — to carry out a wildly ambitious heist idea: getting into the Royal Mint of Spain, and leaving with a freshly printed €984 million.

The addictive, time-hopping narrative makes "Money Heist" a gripping watch, but anyone who enjoys "Lupin" is likely to be particularly taken with the Spanish series' use of heist mechanics to patiently reveal layers of character, backstory, motivation, and conflict among its sprawling ensemble. The emphasis on interpersonal drama proves particularly rewarding here because, unlike "Lupin," "Money Heist" doesn't have a single, clearly defined protagonist; every member of the Professor's crew plays their own crucial part in both the initial heist and its numerous repercussions. That abundance of character texture is one of the reasons why a multi-season "Money Heist" spin-off eventually happened — the other reason being, of course, that "Money Heist" was a massive global hit, at one point second only to "Squid Game" in Netflix viewership metrics for non-English shows.

Ron Howard tells Page Six that what surprised him most about acclaimed photographer Richard Avedon is that he was a lousy student.

“It was kind of interesting to me that he was such a terrible student, had been a merchant marine, and then wound up becoming this remarkable figure in the fashion world,” the Oscar-winning director told us at a special screening of his new Netflix documentary “Avedon,” which is now streaming.

Though not his initial plan, Howard pivoted to focus on the legendary lensman, who died in 2004 at 81 .

“I was just impressed by him and found him so charismatic and entertaining and even courageous,” the filmmaker said of Avedon.

Howard expounded on the photog’s “courage,” explaining that “he was so commercially successful, was afforded so many opportunities, and yet devoted so much of his time to career risks by pursuing issues that were important to him and the nation at that time.”

“Civil rights, Vietnam, the institutional bigotry — he began to use his camera to try to cover and reveal hypocrisy among leadership,” he added.

Howard shared that he was most “surprised” by Avedon’s “American West” project.

entertainment.title: 5 Harry Potter Movie Mistakes The HBO TV Series Could Finally Fix
entertainment.summary: The Harry Potter movies had plenty of magic, but they weren't perfect. Here are five things HBO's upcoming series has the time and room to get right.
entertainment.body:
HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Although the eight "Harry Potter" movies were remarkable, they weren't perfect. The child actors struggled at times, and the revolving door of directors caused a lot of visual inconsistency. The biggest issue, most fans would agree, is how the movies struggled to adapt the increasingly long and complicated source material. "Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix," for instance, is well over 800 pages in most editions. While the movies could adapt the 300-page first book faithfully without much of a struggle, figuring out how to streamline 800 pages seemed to be a massive headache for the writers.

Most of the mistakes featured on this list are related to the movies' time constraints. The upcoming HBO "Harry Potter" series enjoys all the breathing room that comes with the medium of TV, which means it can include so many of the fun subplots and complicated lore that made the books shine. Minor characters like Charlie Weasley who were cut from the movies have already been cast, which is promising news for book fans. Here are five things the "Harry Potter" show can do that the movies didn't.

Aidan Monaghan/HBO A popular complaint from book fans is that the movies do Ron (Rupert Grint) dirty. From "Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban" onward, it seems clear that Hermione (Emma Watson) is the script's favorite. She has most of her rougher edges sanded down. Gone is the bookish, overbearing girl fans loved in the books, replaced with a perpetually competent cool girl with only the occasional neurotic moment.

In the books, Ron is a valuable member of the trio thanks to his native knowledge of the wizarding world, but most of those moments are cut from the movies. Book Ron is the only one who knows what the slur "mudblood" means, for instance, whereas Hermione is already in the know in "Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets." Ron's bravery is also downplayed; in the "Prisoner of Azkaban" book, it's a bruised-up Ron who tells Sirius, "If you want to kill Harry, you'll have to kill us too!" The movie adaptation gives Hermione the line instead.

Ron's worst movie in the series is "Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire," which has enough screen time to cover Ron's fight with Harry and his fight with Hermione, but not enough to cover his more redemptive moments. To movie-only viewers, Ron in "Goblet of Fire" comes across as a huge jerk for most of the run-time; a TV show can give him more nuance.

The film features an all-star voice cast, including Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Abbi Jacobson, Bryan Cranston and Beanie Feldstein.

Despite there being no cure for the progressive brain disorder, Miller Rogen said she and her husband have “found a lot of hope” through their advocacy work.

“At Hilarity for Charity, we’ve learned so much about brain health; we have education to teach people how to keep their brains healthy,” she explained. “And so it’s not as dark as it was. There’s still a lot more work to be done, but there is a lot of hope, which is amazing.”

entertainment.title: 5 Beloved Sitcoms That Started Off Terrible Before Becoming Great
entertainment.summary: Not every series can hit the ground running. In fact, some of the greatest sitcoms of all time would never make it past their first season today.
entertainment.body:
NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Not all sitcoms are created equally. Not every sitcom can complete its entire run without a bad season , some need a little time for characters to gel or storylines to develop before truly hitting their stride. Then there are sitcoms to get off to really rough starts, but somehow manage to turn it around and go on to become some of the most beloved sitcoms of all time.

Depending on the network, competition, and era of television, one bad season could sometimes be enough to get a show canceled. During the height of broadcast television, for instance, networks had to be less forgiving because they couldn't afford to give a show time to figure it out and risk falling behind in the ratings. Now with the rise of streaming, the big networks have become less likely to give a show the axe quickly.

While some sitcoms are beyond saving, others need that extra time for showrunners and writers to have a chance to iron out some details, fine-tune everything and drastically improve the show. In fact, some of the best sitcoms of all time came dangerously close to never materializing at all. Here's our list of five sitcoms that started out terrible, but righted the ship and went on to become legendary.

NBC During its ten year run, "Friends" would become known for its brilliant ensemble cast, how they perfectly interacted with each other, and how their lives all intertwined. That kind of complexity, however, takes time to form and develop. So it's no surprise that the first season of the breakout sitcom comes off a little stilted and awkward.

While it's established right from the beginning that our six leads all know each other and have been friends for a while, they feel more like six acquaintances living six separate lives, as opposed to one cohesive friend group. Early episodes often featured plot lines that only followed one character and their journey, like Rachel leaving her wedding, Monica's push to become a chef or Ross ending up with a pet monkey. As time went on, you started to see more interconnected plots like Chandler and Monica keeping their relationship a secret, or when Monica and Rachel lose their apartment to Chandler and Joey following a heated trivia contest.

Character development was also a little slow to develop. In later seasons, for example, Joey is a lovable dimwit with a burgeoning acting career that was always in flux. In Season 1, however, he comes across as mostly just a generic hunk without many eccentricities. It's a perfect microcosm of the show as a whole. The first season feels plain compared to the hilarity that fans got in later seasons.

entertainment.title: Ben Stiller and Christine Taylor’s real-life romance has a sweet ‘Meet the Parents’ connection
entertainment.summary: The couple married in 2000, separated 17 years later and reconciled during the COVID-19 pandemic.
entertainment.body:
Christine Taylor revealed that her husband, Ben Stiller, pulled off a surprise proposal while filming “Meet the Parents” — and it had a sweet connection to the movie’s plot.

The “Brady Bunch Movie” star told Page Six that Stiller was preparing to pop the question while shooting the 2000 comedy, just as his character, Greg Focker, was planning to do the same.

“The story is simultaneous [with our lives],” Taylor told Page Six at the “Focker-in-Law” premiere on Wednesday. “He was getting ready to propose to me as he was shooting. He was literally asking my dad for my hand in marriage, unbeknownst to me, so it was a little bit of life imitating art.”

“But as Ben has said before, my dad wasn’t quite as intimidating as Bob De Niro’s character!” she joked.

Taylor, 55, revealed that Stiller, 60, surprised her while she was in Los Angeles and she believed he was in New York rehearsing for “Meet the Parents.”

Unbeknownst to her, the “Zoolander” star had flown to LA and arranged for her friends and family to gather at her home while she was at the movies.

“I was driving to my house, and oh, my garage clicker isn’t working, and oh, shoot, I’ve got to park the car and go in the front door, and when I started to walk up the front steps, the door was open, rose petals were lining the rooms,” Taylor remembered.

“He had flown in; my whole family was involved. I couldn’t believe it,” she added. “I really pride myself on…it’s very hard to surprise me, let’s put it that way.”

entertainment.summary: From Cynthia Erivo & Travis Barker doing *the* drum break justice to the Red Hot Chili Peppers donning Rick Rubin wigs, these were our highlights.
entertainment.body:
While many of the headlines leading up to the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony this weekend were about who wouldn’t be there, our highlights from Saturday night’s (Nov. 14) show at L.A.’s Peacock Theatre are all about who showed up and showed out.

The night was bookended by two surprise performances, starting with 2005 inductees U2 playing a brand-new song and a classic to kick things off and ending with 2001 inductees Aerosmith joining forces with 2009 inductees Run-DMC to perform their pioneering rock/hip-hop mash-up “Walk This Way,” a top five Billboard Hot 100 smash in 1986.

In between, a mixture of rising stars and bona fide legends showed up to either introduce or pay musical tribute to the Class of 2026 — or, in some cases, the inductees themselves got in on the action. The full Wu-Tang Clan hit the stage for a medley, while Queen Latifah and MC Lyte joined forces for a joint performance celebrating their contributions as women in hip-hop, Billy Idol and his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens did one solo song and one duet with a famous face, and Peter Hook of Joy Division and New Order was surrounded by superfans for a celebration of his dual groups.

The through-line of the night was innovation. While the Rock Hall has expanded far beyond the genre of rock & roll, each member of the new class has something vital in common: They changed music for generations to come.

Below, find Billboard ‘s best moments from the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, which will air Dec. 8 from 8-11 p.m. ET on ABC and stream on Disney+ the next day.

U2 crashed the Rock Hall ceremony, opening the show with a surprise two-song set a day after releasing their new album, Carnaval De Luz . The band wasn’t on the bill — they were inducted back in 2005, their first year of eligibility — but they kicked off the night with “Silencio,” the album’s second single, joined by a line of performers dressed as riot police and carrying shields, then closed with 1984’s “Pride (In the Name of Love).” The twofer from the Hall of Fame vets set the tone for an evening of legends only.

Newman is best known for his performance as "Brick" Pollitt in "Cat on a Hot Tin Roof," for which he earned the Academy Award nomination for best actor. Other notable projects include "The Hustler," "Hud," "Cool Hand Luke," "Torn Curtain," and "Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid." Newman won the best actor Oscar for Martin Scorsese's "The Color of Money" in 1987. He also won the Golden Globe for his 1969 directorial debut, "Rachel, Rachel," in the best director category, along with a best supporting performance win for the HBO miniseries "Empire Falls."

Static Media "He treated me like he was disappointed in me a lot of the time, and he had every right to be."

The above quote is from a retrospective of Newman's life and career by Vanity Fair . This particular quote, sourced from Newman's 1982 interview with Time, is in reference to his father, Arthur Sigmund Newman.

The Vanity Fair piece notes that Newman's relationship with his father was rather distant, leaving Newman "determined to parent his children differently." Unfortunately, reality didn't line up with intent.

"It has been one of the great agonies of my life that he could never know," Newman added, referring to his accomplishments. "I wanted desperately to show him that somehow, somewhere along the line, I could cut the mustard. And I never got a chance, never got a chance," Newman mused.

entertainment.title: Daniel Hall, Co-Founder of Australian Rock Band Taxiride, Dies at 48
entertainment.summary: The guitarist and singer helped write and record “Get Set,” which won an ARIA Award and reached Billboard’s Modern Rock Tracks chart in 1999.
entertainment.body:
Daniel Hall , a co-founder of the Australian rock band Taxiride , died Friday (Nov. 13). He was 48.

The band announced his death in a social media post. “It is with the heaviest of hearts we announce the passing of our youngest brother in arms, Daniel James Hall,” it read. “We shared some amazing experiences and his departure doesn’t seem real. Rest In Peace Dan.”

In a separate post on Hall’s own page, his partner, Jess, said he died unexpectedly at home in the early hours of Friday. “I am completely devastated,” she wrote. “Your prayers and kind messages are appreciated.” No cause has been given. Related U2 Opens 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Ceremony With Surprise Performance Phil Collins Tells Rock Hall Crowd: 'You Haven't Heard the Last of Me' Filipino Singer Carmelle Storms to Victory in Eurovision Asia Debut in Bangkok Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

Taxiride formed in Melbourne in the late ’90s, after Tim Watson and Tim Wild began writing together and were joined by Jason Singh and Hall, who had spent years busking in the suburb of Camberwell and playing Melbourne venues. The four-piece signed to Warner after recording a demo at the city’s Secret Sound Studios.

Their 1999 debut, Imaginate , produced by Jack Joseph Puig and recorded between Ocean Way in Los Angeles and Secret Sound, went to No. 1 on the ARIA albums chart and was certified double platinum in Australia . It was released in the U.S. on Warner/Sire.

Lead single “Get Set” reached No. 8 on the ARIA singles chart and No. 36 on Billboard’s Modern Rock Tracks chart, and won breakthrough artist – single at the 1999 ARIA Awards . It was also nominated for best pop release. Follow-up “Everywhere You Go” gave the band a second ARIA top 15 hit, and Imaginate drew two further ARIA nominations the following year.

Hall left Taxiride in 2001 to pursue solo work and later formed the band Airway Lanes. He subsequently returned to Taxiride, and the band has continued performing in Australia, with dates still in the diary at the time of his death.

Singh, his former bandmate, said he was “absolutely shattered.” Writing on social media, he said: “R.I.P. my brother Dan Hall. Forever in my soul. Thank you for being one of the hugest parts of my life brother. I’m totally heart broken.”

entertainment.body:
Phil Collins gave a tearful acceptance speech and got an electrifying tribute from Cynthia Erivo, Oprah Winfrey inducted the late Luther Vandross, and Wu-Tang Clan made the Peacock Theater a rowdy celebration at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night.

Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte and Sade were also inducted, and Billy Idol, New Order and Iron Maiden were set to enter the hall later in the evening.

Collins, whose mobility issues and other health problems kept him from performing , took the stage slowly using a pair of canes and cried at a huge ovation from a crowd that included his daughter, actor Lily Collins .

Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker inducted Collins and praised him for his unprecedented dual stardom as a drummer and a hit-making pop singer in the 1980s.

“I grew up just wanting to play the drums,” Collins said. “Everything else has been a really happy accident. I can’t believe, when I look back, how life has gone.”

Barker said Collins’ song “In the Air Tonight” gave the world “arguably the most badass drum fill of all time.”

Minutes later, Barker played that fill himself as Erivo gave a slowed-down, epic rendition of the song that brought the crowd to its feet.

Collins was already in the hall as a member of Genesis, but now gets the solo honor.

Carnaval De Luz , out Friday (Nov. 13) via Interscope, is U2 ’s 16th album and their first full-length of new material since 2017’s Songs of Experience . It was produced by longtime collaborator Jacknife Lee, and its title translates as “Carnival of Light.” The cover, showing the band walking single file along a beach with Bono out front in a top hat, is a clear nod to Abbey Road .

The album closes with “Torn,” a duet with Dolly Parton that her representative has confirmed is her final recorded vocal performance. Parton died in August at 80. U2 wrote the song with Parton and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, and have described it as a country song about broken family ties.

The release also gives U2 a shot at extending a Billboard 200 record. Songs of Experience was their eighth No. 1, making them the only group to top the chart in four consecutive decades. They’ve also notched two Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s, both from 1987’s The Joshua Tree . Carnaval De Luz ’s first-week numbers will be reflected on the Billboard 200 dated Nov. 28.

It’s been a busy 50th anniversary year for the band, who also released two six-song EPs, Days of Ash and Easter Lily , and played a surprise street show on Dublin’s Grafton Street in September. The Edge has called the new album “a messy, provocative, sacred collection of songs,” while Bono promised “loud guitars, deep bass, some ecstatic rhythms.”

entertainment.title: Richard Sterban, longtime bass singer for the Oak Ridge Boys, dead at 83
entertainment.summary: Ahead of joining the Oak Ridge Boys, Sterban worked as a backup singer for Elvis Presley.
entertainment.body:
Richard Sterban, longtime bass singer for the Grammy-winning Oak Ridge Boys, has died. He was 83.

Sterban died Saturday at his home in Hendersonville, Tenn., from complications of bronchitis and pneumonia following a long battle with cancer, according to a statement from his family and the band’s rep .

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers. Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus,” his family said in a statement.

Sterban was forced to step away from touring with the quartet in 2025 due to health issues, but reunited with the group in January 2026 to perform their 1981 hit “Elvira” at the Grand Ole Opry.

Born in 1943 in Camden, NJ, Sterban grew up in nearby Collingswood and began singing in Sunday school at age 6 as a soprano, before his voice dropped to the deep bass that became his trademark.

Sterban graduated from Collingswood High School and went on to study music at Trenton State College, now known as the College of New Jersey.

Sterban moved to Nashville in 1970, where he worked as a backup singer for Elvis Presley.

He left the job in 1972 to join the Oak Ridge Boys, alongside lead singer Duane Allen, baritone William Lee Golden and tenor Joe Bonsall.

sports.title: Dolphins, Colts will stage a "someone has to win" game
sports.summary: The Colts need a lot more than a horseshoe to turn their season around.
sports.body:
Both teams are struggling to say the least. Via NBC Sports research, the 1-7 Dolphins rank 31st in scoring offense, with 15.8 points per game. They’re also 28th in total offense, at 282.3 yards per game.

The Dolphins have been held to 13 or fewer points in five games this season. That’s the most in the league.

And they’re starting Kyle McCord at quarterback, because Malik Willis is on injured reserve.

The Colts haven’t been much better. They’ve lost five in a row since starting the season 2-2. Since Week 12 of the 2025 season, they’re 2-14. That’s the worst record over that span in the entire league.

So, yes, someone has to win. Unless there’s a tie. Which would complicate the four-official road trip to Cincinnati.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Mayfield has been dealing with a lower-leg injury that he suffered in the team’s Week 9 loss to the Bears. Mayfield did not leave the 27-24 loss, but Garafolo reports that he has been in a walking boot at times this week.

While Mayfield’s availability for next weekend’s game in Detroit is in question, he is not expected to miss extended time as a result of the injury. That’s good news for the Buccaneers as their 3-6 record leaves them without too much room to drop more games while remaining in the race for the NFC South title.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels started three games while Mayfield was out with a dislocated thumb and he would be in line to start again if Mayfield is unable to go.

sports.title: Four officials in all will make the road trip from Indy to Cincinnati
sports.summary: It's officially a road trip.
sports.body:
The chaos caused by Friday’s nationwide ground stop prompted the NFL to get very creative with its officiating assignments. That creativity includes four officials getting in a car and traveling from Indianapolis to Cincinnati to work a doubleheader separated by 110 miles.

Via Aditi Kinkhabwala of CBS, backup referee Don Willard will be joined by umpire Terry Killens (pictured), field judge Jabir Walker, and side judge Justin Larrew in the effort to officiate two games in one day: Dolphins-Colts and Steelers-Bengals.

Per the league, not at least since 1970 has an official worked two games in one day.

The full scope of the changes to the usual crew won’t be publicly known until the games are completed and the official Game Books are posted by the league; each one includes the full list of officials by position.

It there are glitches, some will ask why the NFL resorted to such an extreme plan to ensure that there will be enough officials at every game. They use crews for a reason. On Sunday, those crews apparently will be obliterated.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs totals 171 yards in first half as Lions roll over Patriots
sports.summary: For the second consecutive week, the Patriots' defense is having a rough game.
sports.body:
Gibbs has 171 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown as the Lions have cruised to a 21-3 lead late in the second quarter. Gibbs has 13 carries for 93 yards and a touchdown, plus another four catches for 78 receiving yards. The Patriots’ defense has had no answer for him.

It’s the second consecutive ugly outing for New England’s defense, which was shredded by the Packers’ passing game last week.

The Patriots’ offense is also struggling, but that appears to be mostly due to the injury suffered by quarterback Drake Maye on New England’s opening possession. The Patriots had been marching down the field until Maye was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson on third-and-goal, and Maye was knocked out of the game with an ankle injury. After the field goal immediately following that sack, the Patriots haven’t scored.

It’s hard to imagine the Patriots mounting a second-half comeback with Tommy DeVito at the helm, but that’s what they’ll have to do if they’re going to avoid heading home from Germany on a two-game losing streak.

sports.title: Drake Maye limps to locker room, Tommy DeVito in at QB for Patriots in Germany
sports.summary: Maye was injured when Aidan Hutchinson sacked him. Hutchinson was also injured while celebrating the sack.
sports.body:
On a third-and-goal, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson took Maye down and appeared to land on his legs. Maye was slow to get up but walked off the field on his own, and there was initially no indication that he was seriously injured.

But at the start of the Patriots’ second drive, Maye limped to the locker room and backup Tommy DeVito came in to replace him. The Patriots said Maye is questionable to return with an ankle injury.

Hutchinson was also injured while celebrating his sack of Maye, and he’s currently in the locker room as well. The Lions said Hutchinson is questionable to return with a knee injury.

Patriots right tackle Morgan Moses has also left the game with an injury.

The Lions have an early 7-3 lead, but the injuries to two of the best players in the NFL may prove to matter more to both teams’ playoff hopes than the result of this game.

sports.title: Demarvion Overshown wasn't fined for running onto field in street clothes
sports.summary: In the fourth quarter of a Week 9 game the Cowboys led by only three points, Dallas forced — and recovered — a fumble by Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
sports.body:
Said referee Clay Martin in announcing the specific of theinfraction, “Unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas, who had a non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate.”

The non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and the stocking cap was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive for the game due to injury.

While violations of the celebration rules routinely spark fines, Overshown was not financially penalized by the league.

It’s possible Overshown got some sort of punishment from the team, especially since owner and G.M. Jerry Jones rejected Overshown’s claim that he didn’t know it was against the rules for a player not in uniform to run onto the field for a celebration.

“ I don’t think that ,” Jones said. “I really don’t. I think that he’s been involved in football at Texas, and he’s been involved here, and he knows that, at every level, a nonparticipant can’t run out on the field.”

Every player should have known the rule before last Sunday. Given what happened in the Dallas game, where the lost 15 yards of field position set the stage for a game-tying field goal by the Colts (the Cowboys eventually won, 27-23), there’s even less of an excuse to not know it now.

sports.body: If you’ve been a part of Buffalo Rumblings for a bit now, you’re likely familiar with our weekly Reacts polls. Well, once again, we asked your thoughts about the Buffalo Bills and you reacted! Things are pretty darn good in Bills Country these days, thanks to Buffalo’s 7-1 record and current place atop the list in the AFC playoff list. There are a lot of games left to play, but if the season ended today, the Bills would have earned the number-one seed and a bye week to begin the playoffs. Remember, all this is happening while the team navigates a first-time head coach in Joe Brady, and a first-time NFL defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. Buffalo’s offense is legit, ranking first in the NFL in points per game (32.0) and also No. 1 in total yards per game (386.4). As for the defense, it’s appears to be turning the right corners, improving to a middle-of-the-pack unit overall since the bye week. That’s after spending a bulk of the early season among the worst defenses in the league. Quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook III have once again put the NFL on notice, which is of course due in no small measure to the team’s offensive line and a bevy of skill players who are equally interested in blocking defenders into tomorrow on any snap. Is 7-1 a surprise? Likely not given Allen. Yet it’s still worth wondering how much leeway Brady and the new coaching staff should get in their first season, even considering Allen. It’s worth noting Buffalo’s recent favorable stretch of games against backup and emergency quarterbacks. That shouldn’t excuse away their legitimacy as a Super Bowl contender. Good teams defeat bad teams, and the Bills have done that without little problem. Impressively, Buffalo is the only undefeated road team (4-0) left in the NFL this season. Winning is tough in general, but doing so on the road presents teams with the final boss of football challenges. If our latest poll results are any indication, confidence is contagious. Bills Mafia has bought in — no strings attached. Footage from WRAL shows Belichick involved in the effort to clean up the mess, pulling several of his players away from the fray.

The next question is whether discipline will be issued, by the individual teams or the ACC. No penalties were enforced, because the game ended in the early stages of the altercation.

sports.title: With trade offers rejected, Titans' plans for Tony Pollard come into question
sports.summary: All the factors had lined up for a Tony Pollard trade.
sports.body:
At 1-7, the Titans aren’t contenders. Pollard is in the final year of his contract. While a compensatory draft pick becomes possible in 2028 (depending on Tennessee’s 2027 free-agent acquisitions and losses), the Titans could have gotten a draft pick in 2027 if they’d traded him.

What could they have gotten? As we hear it, they turned down a fourth-round pick and a player. (The Packers and the Broncos were the two teams linked to Pollard .)

So what’s the plan for Pollard? Maybe they want to keep Pollard beyond 2026. He’s in the last season of a three-year, $21.75 million deal. He’s making $7.25 million this year.

And Pollard is on track for his fifth straight 1,000-yard season. He’s not even in the top 20 highest-paid running backs by annual average. The franchise tag at the position for 2027 is expected to be in the range of $15 million.

Pollard will be 30 in April. That makes it harder to put a proper number on his next contract. But if the Titans weren’t willing to take the best offer they could get for him, it suggests that they have a plan premised on potentially signing him to a new contract.

The decision to keep Pollard could be as simple as the Titans not being confident in their alternatives. Pollard has 147 touches in eight games. His backup, Tajae Spears, has 33 in six games. Rookie Nick Singleton has seven in four games. Julius Chestnut has no touches in eight games.

The answer could be that simple. The Titans had insufficient confidence in their other options if Pollard was traded. Which would have complicated the ongoing effort to develop quarterback Cam Ward.

Regardless, the Titans had a chance to get something now (we don’t know the name of the player that was offered; it could have been a running back) and a 2027 draft pick by trading Pollard. They decided not to.

sports.title: 49ers will fly to Colorado tonight to begin acclimating to altitude for Mexico City game

“I think it helps,” Shanahan said. “I grew up mainly in Denver, and I know how bad it would be for me. No matter how good of shape you’re in, you come home from college and you run up the stairs and you’re out of breath. It takes some time to get used to altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver it’s always a challenge, and Mexico City is higher than Denver. It’s not make or break, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better.”

Shanahan thanked Air Force head coach Troy Calhoun for allowing the 49ers to use his team’s practice facility in Colorado Springs, as he did before the 49ers’ Mexico City game in 2022. Air Force’s Falcon Stadium is at 6,621 feet. Estadio Azteca has an altitude of 7,280 feet — exactly 2,000 feet higher than Denver’s Mile High elevation.

Next Sunday night will be the 49ers’ second international game of the season. They opened the season in Australia, where their decision to arrive a week early to get used to the time difference was credited as one of the reasons for their impressive performance against the Rams. Now they hope another weeklong preparation will yield similar results.

sports.title: Arch Manning shakes off 3 interceptions, throws game-winning TD pass as Texas beats LSU
sports.summary: As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday.
sports.body:
After throwing three interceptions and seeing his team fall behind LSU 21-10, Manning turned it on late, culminating in a 12-play, 58-yard drive that saw Manning throw the game-winning touchdown pass with three seconds remaining as Texas won 22-21.

“That’s what college football is all about,” Manning said after the game.

Manning’s numbers were not impressive: 19-of-35 for 174 yards and one touchdown with three interceptions and four sacks, plus 35 yards and a touchdown running. But when Texas needed him to march the offense down the field at the end of the game, he did it. His touchdown pass to Raleek Brown was a perfectly placed ball, and he also ran for two first downs on the game-winning drive.

For No. 6 Texas, the win means they’ll almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, as they’ll be heavy favorites the next two weeks against Arkansas and Texas A&M. For LSU, the loss knocks first-year coach Lane Kiffin out of playoff contention.

Manning, the scion of the first family of quarterbacks, will have an opportunity do what neither his grandfather Archie nor his uncles Peyton and Eli ever did: Win a national championship.

sports.title: Lions, Jets renegotiated Andre Cisco trade after concerns arose about his physical
sports.summary: The Broncos-Chargers Daiyan Henley trade wasn't the only one affected by the player's physical.
sports.body:
The Lions also told the Jets they wanted to change the terms of their trade for safety Andre Cisco after concerns about his physical. But unlike the Chargers, the Jets agreed to it, and the Lions ultimately sent the Jets a 2029 sixth-round pick for Cisco after initially agreeing to give up a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Tom Pelissero reports that the modified terms were based on medical concerns. There’s no word on what those concerns were, but Lions coach Dan Campbell said the plan is for Cisco to play on Sunday against the Patriots.

The Jets went along with the Lions’ request, and in the scheme of things the difference between a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 sixth-round pick is minor. Still, it points to an inherent flaw in the NFL’s trade rules: The team acquiring a player has the ability to go back on the trade, or negotiate better terms, after the trade deadline. That puts the team trading the player in a difficult position: After you’ve already told a player you’re trading him, and told another player you’re signing him or bringing him up from the practice squad to take his place, you don’t want to go back on that. So if the team you’re trading with tells you, “We didn’t like his physical, so we’ll back out of the trade unless you take less compensation,” you may feel you have no choice but to accept.

The NFL could resolve that by not allowing trades to be renegotiated after the deadline: Either the player passes the physical and the trade goes through, or the player fails the physical and the trade does not go through. No more half measures like, “We failed him on his physical, but we’ll pass the physical if you agree to take a lesser draft pick for him.”

Another solution could be that physicals for traded players are conducted by an independent, league-appointed doctor, rather than the team’s medical staff. If that doctor says the player passes the physical, the team trading for the player can’t back out.

The Jets and Chargers had different reactions to their trade partners asking to renegotiate the trades, but the situation both teams were faced with highlights potential problems that can arise with the NFL allowing teams to change the terms of trades after the trade deadline.

sports.title: Three referees will be working in other roles on Sunday, due to the ground stop

Via Ben Austro of FootballZebras.com, three referees will be working in other roles on Sunday.

Referee Carl Cheffers and referee Alex Kemp will work as umpires. Referee Shawn Hochuli (pictured) will work as a back judge.

The reconfiguration resulted from the NFL’s decision to assign officials to games within driving distance of their homes.

Austro also notes that the replay officials for all Sunday games will work out of NFL headquarters. They were in Detroit on Friday for an all-day, in-person training session. Instead of fanning out to the various game locations, they all went to New York.

It sets the stage for a potentially strange day, with any mistakes inevitably being blamed on the inability of the NFL to get the officials where they needed to be. If it works, however, it could prompt the NFL to reconsider the overall staffing plan, if there’s a way to do it that reduces expenses.

I think that’s a tongue-in-cheek remark. I hope it’s a tongue-in-cheek remark.

Either way, Sunday could get interesting. The players and coaches have gotten to where they’re supposed to be. The officials haven’t, and the deck has been dramatically reshuffled in order to ensure that each game will be properly staffed.

sports.summary: Saturday's not alright for fighting.
sports.body:
But a fight nevertheless happened at the end of the game between Louisville and Bill Belichick’s North Carolina Tar Hells.

The Cardinals led, 16-14, with time ticking away. (UNC had a timeout remaining but hadn’t used it on the final Louisville drive, after a game-sealing interception.) Louisville received the snap and took a knee as the clock hit 15 seconds.

North Carolina, despite not using its final timeout, deployed the Schiano-style effort to blow up victory formation. Which sparked a shoving match match between opposing lineman. Which eventually became a full-blown brawl.

Through it all, time expired and the game ended. It will be interesting to see whether the ACC or the individual schools hand out suspensions as a result of the fracas.

The loss dropped North Carolina to 5-5. The Tar Heels need one win in remaining games against Virginia and NC State to become bowl-eligible in Belichick’s second season on the job.

And that could be harder to do against Virginia next week, if one or more UNC players end up being required to sit out.

New York has a stronger team right now than they had at the end of last year, but there’s still a big gulf between them and the 7-1 Bills. All indications for this one are brutal. The Jets’ current losing streak has been by an average of 9.5 points per game, while the Bills’ winning streak has been by an average of 12.3 points per game. Specifically, this Jets/Bills matchup in the Aaron Glenn era is way worse: The Bills have won by an average of 23.5(!) points. The second matchup didn’t even include Josh Allen; he was a healthy scratch, and they still handed the Jets a 35-8 loss. In Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport’s trade deadline notebook, they wrote on Buffalo’s interest in Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates, both of whom were dealt to the Jaguars: > “The Jaguars and Bills will be in competition to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl, but both were in competition for some of the same players ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. > The two teams that were most aggressive in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis were the Bills and Jaguars, who wound up trading a first- and second-round pick to the Eagles. > The two teams most aggressive for former Falcons safety Jessie Bates also were the Bills and Jaguars, who traded second- and fifth-round picks to Atlanta.” They later went on to write that after the Jaguars trades, the Bills pivoted to Cardinals safety Budda Baker and Hooker. sports.body: The Jets’ defense has had its issues in 2026, to say the least. However, there’s at least one area where they have improved. The defense as a whole has been a lot more opportunistic this year in terms of forcing fumbles. Led by David Bailey’s five, they have forced a total of 13 fumbles. That’s already four more than the total for all of last season. New York’s fumble luck has been a lot better too, as they’ve recovered 50 percent of all fumbles. This is much higher than their 2025 percentage, which was the second-worst in the league at 35 percent (and was actually on target to break the all-time record until they had a few over the last few weeks of the season). Had they been closer to 50 percent last year, or 2023 when they were dead last in fumble recovery percentage, or 2022 when they were 30th, those seasons could arguably have played out very differently. 2023 in particular was particularly galling, as the Jets started 7-4 and then lost their last six as the turnovers dried up. They almost tied the all-time NFL record for the fewest defensive fumble recoveries until Carl Lawson ended a nine-game drought by recovering one with two games remaining. In the end, they only managed to recover 21 percent of fumbles by opposing offenses. It’s often been debated how much of fumble recovery percentages are dictated by talent and how much is based on luck, with most analytical studies concluding it’s mostly luck. However, if you have a team that is hungry and hustles to the ball, has players who are particularly adept at possessing loose balls or are creating the kinds of fumbles which are more likely to be recovered by the defense, this obviously has an effect on some level. Regardless, at least the Jets have seemingly started to regress to the mean in this area. So the next question becomes when will they start to do anything impactful with these recoveries? That was Muhammad Wilkerson, on a play where Mike DeVito had forced the ball loose on a sack of Russell Wilson. That’s a pretty remarkable statistic.
